pre_score_amendments.reason: canonical corpus pin is not byte-reproducible on the local Windows CPU runtime

pre_score_amendments.finding: a contraction rewrite such as "are not" to "aren't" costs two word-level edit operations (substitute plus delete), so even a semantically faithful, rules-only transformation of a short source reaches a word edit rate near 0.27; the original 0.15 gate would fail rows for reasons unrelated to the research question
pre_score_amendments.reason: word edit rate gate was set below the mechanical floor of the ruleset before any scoring

pre_score_amendments.change: gates now bind to characters INTRODUCED by the transformation (present in transformed, absent from source alphabet): introduced characters must be ASCII and must include no Cc, Cf, Mn, Mc, Me, Zl, Zp, or non-space Zs codepoint; pre-existing source codepoints are reported without gating
pre_score_amendments.finding: the audit gated on absolute presence of category Cc characters in transformed text, which flags ordinary newlines (U+000A) that the GPT-2 source generation already contains; 28 of 32 development rows failed a gate that measures the corpus, not the candidate
pre_score_amendments.reason: codepoint audit scope error found on development robustness evidence before confirmation scoring
